marks.gloss_en: ואזדא רבא לטעמיה, דאמר רבא: מים על גבי מים היינו הנחתן
Rava: water on top of water -- that is its resting
ממאי? מדאמר מר: תוך ארבע אמות עמד לפוש פטור, לכתף חייב... -- only stopping to rest is a placing
Abaye: provided he stood [still] to rest
אלא אמר רבא: כגון שקלט מעל גבי גומא (= p_rava_gumma); R' Chiyya b. Rav Huna's wall (5a.18) falls on the way -- see obj_ha_lo_nach and obj_mayim_lo_nayechi
Rava: where he caught [the rainwater] from atop a pit [of water]

אימור דאמר רבא בספר, דעביד דנייח; מים מי עבידי דנייחי?! -- a scroll rests on a slope, water does not; this knocks down a_kotel_meshupa (targeted at the okimta it rescued -- see header). Unanswered: אלא אמר רבא
ואמר רבא: בכותל משופע -- the scroll rests on a sloped wall (= p_rava_kotel_meshupa)
Rava: [the scroll mishnah speaks of] a sloped wall [on which the scroll rests]
והוינן בה: אמאי הופכו על הכתב? הא לא נח! -- the scroll has not come to rest in the public domain, so rolling it back would be no lifting
the mishnah: one reading on the roof whose scroll rolled from his hand -- once it reached ten handbreadths [of the public domain] he turns it over onto its writing [and may not roll it back]
oil floating on wine [is it resting, for lifting?] is the dispute of R' Yochanan ben Nuri and the Rabbis
one laden with food and drink who goes in and out all day is not liable until he stands still
one who moved objects from corner to corner, then changed his mind and carried them out, is exempt, for the lifting was not from the outset for this
בשלמא בן עזאי, קסבר מהלך כעומד דמי -- walking through the colonnade is as if he stood there
אלא רבנן, נהי נמי דקסברי מהלך לאו כעומד דמי, היכא אשכחנא כהאי גוונא דחייב? -- where do we find one liable when the object passes through a place of exemption?
Ben Azzai holds that one walking is like one standing
one who carries out from a shop to a plaza by way of a colonnade is liable
